title: Changing from bass violin to slide trombone
summary: He moved from bass violin to slide trombone at Welch's urging because it was more exciting; talk of bass parts.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Did you say you, say something about when you changed from bass violin to...
Yes, you traded your bass as on...

We were, I was with several lead bands when I was trading from trombone, bass violin to trombone. See, we had the old man who was a key trombone player, you know. But in the beginning, when he came in the band, but after he was with us a while, he went back to the bass violin, you see, then he took the bass violin and I played trombone because Mr. Wells said that he thought the slight trombone was more exciting among the people and what they would have trombone. And I think so too and we went along pretty good.
It kind of looks more exciting.
Yeah, it was something new, different.
Did you play about the same kind of a part on the slide as they used on the valve? No, you had a little more white cut.

But it wasn't nothing like now, you know, not the slight trombone, nothing now. But it was a little bit different from the valve trombone. But you see at that time it was more sliding, the thing they get was more exciting, you see. But those guys now is cutting them trombone like a cronet player. Oh yeah.
You play mainly bass parts, I guess.
Bass parts, that's right. I think they play mostly the bass parts.
